messages.content:
You read one job posting and list what it asks of applicants. You write JSON only.

Rules:
1. Instructions are in English. The posting may be in Finnish, Swedish or English. Write every output text in plain English.
2. Each posting sentence has a label like [P6]. For every requirement, give the number of the ONE sentence it comes from in "sentence".
3. List only what the posting asks of the applicant: skills, tools, languages, education, experience, licences. Do not list duties, benefits or facts about the company.
4. One requirement per distinct ask. At most 12. "text" is a short English phrase, at most 80 characters. Never include the employer's name.
5. "kind" is "must" when the sentence or its heading uses words like: edellytämme, edellytyksenä, vaadimme, sinulla on, hallitset, odotamme, required, must, you have, requirements, krav. "kind" is "nice" for: eduksi, katsotaan eduksi, arvostamme, plussaa, toivomme, nice to have, a plus, preferred, meriterande. If there is no such word, use "nice".
6. "category" is one of: skill, language, education, experience, authorisation, other.
   - language: a working language. Put the ISO code in "language" (fi, sv, en, ...).
   - experience: years or prior work. Put the number of years in "years" if stated.
   - authorisation: licence, certificate, card, security clearance, registration, work permit.
   - other: soft or vague asks such as "team player" or "stress tolerance".
7. "esco": up to 3 ids from the ESCO list (like "K4") that name the same skill. Only for skill, experience and education. Use [] if none fits. Never invent ids.
8. "statutory": "law" if the requirement is set by law for this job (public-sector language rules, licensed professions, security clearance, criminal record check, work permit), else "none".
9. "questionType": choose one, else "none":
   - "language": a must-have language requirement, and the work could plausibly start in another language. Never for English when the posting is written in English.
   - "years": a must-have number of years, 3 or more.
   - "degree": a must-have degree.
   - "tool": a must-have specific product or version where a comparable tool may transfer.
   - "vague": a vague or soft ask.
   Use "none" when statutory is "law".
10. "question": one polite question TO THE EMPLOYER that invites them to reconsider, following the pattern for its type. Never say the requirement is wrong, unnecessary, unrealistic or biased. No numbers except the years from the posting. null when questionType is "none".
   - language: "Is Finnish needed from day one, or could someone start in English and build up Finnish on the job?"
   - years: "Would someone who has done <work>, with fewer than <N> years, be worth a conversation?"
   - degree: "Would hands-on experience in <field> work instead of the degree?"
   - tool: "Would experience with a comparable tool be enough, if the person learns <tool> on the job?"
   - vague: "What does '<phrase>' look like in this job? One concrete example helps us find people who have done it."
11. "why": one neutral sentence, at most 140 characters, no numbers, saying what in the posting prompted the question. null when there is no question.
12. Never turn age, gender, nationality, ethnicity, religion, health, family status or appearance into a requirement. If a sentence asks for one, put its number in "dropped". "Native speaker", "mother tongue" and "experience in Finland" count as nationality: never write them in "text"; name the language level or the work instead.
13. "title": the role in plain English, at most 60 characters. "summary": at most 2 sentences about the work, no employer name.
14. Every requirement has all of these keys: text, kind, category, sentence, esco, language, years, statutory, questionType, question, why. Use null for language, years, question and why when they do not apply.

Posting language: en
Posting title: R&D Director
Work languages listed by the source: en

Posting sentences:
[P0] At Kuori, we build heavy-duty outdoor displays, touchscreens, and payment terminals engineered to survive real-world chaos - without failing when weather or high usage hits.
[P1] We've grown from a Finnish startup into a global player with hardware running in over 30 countries, outmanoeuvring sluggish industry giants through speed, mass customisation, and Finnish grit (_sisu_).
[P2] We are looking for a driven, fast-thinking R&D Director to lead our hardware engineering efforts.
[P3] Reporting directly to our CTO, you will have total autonomy to make critical technical decisions, clear obstacles for our engineering teams, and drive product execution as we scale.
[P4] If you run towards accountability and want to shape heavy-duty hardware instead of fighting corporate bureaucracy, this is your invitation to build something great.
[P5] In your daily work, you will:
[P6] Drive product execution across the entire development lifecycle -taking hardware smoothly from initial concept and prototyping through to mass production.
[P7] Lead, mentor, and empower our engineering teams, building an environment where people take pride in their work and perform at their best.
[P8] Make autonomous decisions and proactively resolve bottlenecks to keep technical execution aligned with business goals.
[P9] Maintain control over project timelines, budgets, and technical resources when deadlines tighten.
[P10] Foster seamless cross-functional alignment between your teams, manufacturing, operations, and quality assurance.
[P11] Implement feedback loops and fast problem-solving practices to continuously elevate product quality and technical maturity.
[P12] What we expect from you:
[P13] A builder mindset - you thrive in a company environment where (almost) nothing is set, but everything is possible
[P14] A growth attitude - you enjoy challenges and embrace opportunities for personal and professional development
[P15] Hands-on approach: you are not afraid to take action, dive into the work and carry responsibility.
[P16] You spot what needs to be done and take independent responsibility and deliver results
[P17] Broad technical understanding across mechanics and electronics, with the ability to challenge technical decisions, connect disciplines, and make informed trade-offs.
[P18] Proven track record of owning outcomes and leading technical teams through high-pressure phases.
[P19] A genuine curiosity and practical knack for leveraging modern AI tools to streamline R&D processes, speed up technical workflows, and cut out administrative friction.
[P20] 15+ years of relevant work experience in engineering and hardware product development.
[P21] This role requires weekly onsite work at our headquarters in Espoo, Finland, to stay close to hardware prototyping, manufacturing, and engineering teams
[P22] Professional working fluency in English (fluent Finnish is not required).
[P23] What we offer:
[P24] A chance to customise your career and grow in your field in a rapidly growing high-tech company
[P25] Direct line to our CTO and C-level in a low-hierarchy, entrepreneurial environment.
[P26] Unlike legacy hardware giants, you won't fight through five layers of committees and red tape just to ship an engineering fix-our short decision paths mean
[P27] smart ideas always beat corporate bureaucracy.
[P28] An international and easy-going team of 70 bright minds who embrace a culture of humour and collaboration
[P29] Full-time, permanent contract with clear room to expand your leadership footprint as Kuori scales.
[P30] Sounds like your next challenge?
[P31] We encourage you to apply promptly.
[P32] We are looking for the absolute best person for the role - so if that means we need to wait for you to relocate to
[P33] Finland, we are more than willing to wait for the right fit.
[P34] Apply now - let's build something extraordinary together.
